“他是个好天主教徒；他为此受过苦；在‘永贞之岛’，这就是一纸通行证。他爬得很高；他是哈瓦那海事法庭的法官。所以今天他在这裡，在这移交海盗的事裡陪着我伯父。我伯父非常爱他。奥布赖恩起先是我伯父的书记，我伯父把他捧成了法官，他还是我伯父田庄的总管，在我伯父的裡奥梅迪奥（Rio Medio）城影响很大。我告诉你，你若来看我们，最好同奥布赖恩法官先生搞好关系。我伯父年纪很大了，我若死在他前头，我想这奥布赖恩到头来会娶我表妹，因为我那可怜的伯父大权旁落在他手裡。另有几个觊觎的人，可他们没什么机会，因为到我伯父的裡奥梅迪奥城来实在太危险——因为这人的阴谋诡计，也因为他对民众的势力。”

我凝视着卡洛斯。那城的名字我本觉得耳熟。此刻我猛然想起来，那正是尼古拉斯·埃尔·德莫尼奥——那位名声大得近乎神话的海盗——击退罗利海军上将（Admiral Rowley）艇队的地方。

“来吧，你最好见见这位想这么抬举我们的爱尔兰贵人，”——他莫测地瞥了我一眼——“不过在我伯父醒来之前，别大声说话。”

他推开门。我随他进了那间屋子——老堂与他女儿那迷人的身影，片刻之前才退进去的。

### III / 三
===Original===

The room was very lofty and coldly dim; there were great bars in front of the begrimed windows. It was very bare, containing only a long black table, some packing cases, and half a dozen rocking chairs. Of these, five were very new and one very old, black and heavy, with a green leather seat and a coat of arms worked on its back cushions. There were little heaps of mahogany sawdust here and there on the dirty tiled floor, and a pile of sacking in one corner. Beneath a window the flap of an open trapdoor half hid a large green damp-stain; a deep recess in the wall yawned like a cavern, and had two or three tubs in the right corner; a man with a blond head, slightly bald as if he had been tonsured, was rocking gently in one of the new chairs.
Opposite him, with his aged face towards us, sat the old Don asleep in the high chair. His delicate white hands lay along the arms, one of them holding a gold vinaigrette; his black, silver-headed cane was between his silk-stockinged legs. The diamond buckles of his shoes shot out little vivid rays, even in that gloomy place. The young girl was sitting with her hands to her temples and her elbows on the long table, minutely examining the motionlessness of a baby lizard, a tiny thing with golden eyes, whom fear seemed to have turned into stone.
We entered quietly, and after a moment she looked up candidly into my eyes, and placed her finger on her lips, motioning her head towards her father. She placed her hand in mine, and whispered very clearly:
“Be welcome, my English cousin,” and then dropped her eyes again to the lizard.
She knew all about me from Carlos. The man of whom I had seen only the top of his head, turned his chair suddenly and glinted at me with little blue eyes. He was rather small and round, with very firm flesh, and very white, plump hands. He was dressed in the black clothes of a Spanish judge. On his round face there was always a smile like that which hangs around the jaws of a pike﻿—only more humorous. He bowed a little exaggeratedly to me and said:
“Ah, ye are that famous Mr. Kemp.”
I said that I imagined him the more famous Señor Juez O’Brien.
“It’s little use saying ye arren’t famous,” he said. His voice had the faint, infinitely sweet twang of certain Irishry; a thing as delicate and intangible as the scent of lime flowers.

===Chinese===

那房间高旷而冷清昏暗；污黑的窗前装着粗铁栏。屋裡空空荡荡，只有一张黑色长桌、几只货箱和六把摇椅。其中五把很新，一把很旧，黑沉沉的沉重，绿皮坐垫，靠背垫上绣着纹章。肮脏的瓷砖地上这儿那儿堆着一小堆一小堆红木锯屑，一角堆着麻袋。一扇活板门敞开的翻板下面，半掩着一大块绿色的潮渍；墙上一个深凹的壁龛张着口像座洞穴，右角裡摆着两三只桶；一个金发脑袋的人——微微秃顶，像受过剃发礼——正坐在一把新摇椅裡轻轻摇晃。

他对面，老堂睡在高背椅裡，苍老的脸朝着我们。他纤秀的白手搭在扶手上，一只握着金香盒；黑手杖银头，夹在他丝袜裹着的两膝之间。鞋上的钻石扣针幽幽地迸出细小的光芒，即便在这样昏暗的地方。年轻的姑娘双手支着太阳穴，臂肘撑在长桌上，细细端详着一只小蜥蜴的死寂——一个金眼睛的小东西，恐惧似乎把它变成了石头。

我们悄悄进去，片刻后她坦率地抬眼望进我的眼睛，把一根手指抵在唇上，朝她父亲那边偏了偏头。她把手放进我手裡，非常清晰地低语：

“欢迎你，我的英国表兄。”随后又垂下眼睛看蜥蜴。

关于我的一切她都从卡洛斯那裡知道了。那个我只见过头顶的人忽然转过椅子，一双小小的蓝眼睛朝我闪了闪。他相当矮小滚圆，肉很紧实，一双手又白又胖。他穿着西班牙法官的黑衣裳。圆脸上永远挂着一丝微笑，像狗鱼腮边挂的那种——只是更幽默些。他向我略带夸张地欠了欠身，说：

“啊，您就是那位有名的肯普先生。”

我说，我猜想他才是更有名的奥布赖恩法官先生（Señor Juez O’Brien）。

“说自己不出名，没什么用处，”他说。他的嗓音裡带着某种爱尔兰腔的微弱的、无限甜润的鼻音；一件像菩提花香一样精致缥缈的东西。

===Original===

“Our noble friend”﻿—he indicated Carlos with a little flutter of one white hand﻿—“has told me what make of a daredevil gallant ye are; breaking the skulls of half the Bow Street runners for the sake of a friend in distress. Well, I honour ye for it; I’ve done as much myself.” He added, “In the old days,” and sighed.
“You mean in the ’98,” I said, a little insolently.
O’Brien’s eyes twinkled. He had, as a matter of fact, nearly lost his neck in the Irish fiasco, either in Clonmel or Sligo, bolting violently from the English dragoons, in the mist, to a French man-of-war’s boats in the bay. To him, even though he was now a judge in Cuba, it was an episode of heroism of youth﻿—of romance, in fact. So that, probably, he did not resent my mention of it. I certainly wanted to resent something that was slighting in his voice, and patronizing in his manner.
The old Don slumbered placidly, his face turned up to the distant begrimed ceiling.
“Now, I’ll make you a fair offer,” O’Brien said suddenly, after an intent study of the insolent glance that I gave him. I disliked him because I knew nothing about the sort of man he was. He was, as a matter of fact, more alien to me than Carlos. And he gave me the impression that, if perhaps he were not absolutely the better man, he could still make a fool of me, or at least make me look like a fool.
“I’m told you are a Separationist,” he said. “Well, it’s like me. I am an Irishman; there has been a price on my head in another island. And there are warrants out against you here for assaulting the admiral. We can work together, and there’s nothing low in what I have in mind for you.”
He had heard frequently from Carlos that I was a desperate and aristocratically lawless young man, who had lived in a district entirely given up to desperate and murderous smugglers. But this was the first I had heard definitely of warrants against me in Jamaica. That, no doubt, he had heard from Ramon, who knew everything. In all this little sardonic Irishman said to me, it seemed the only thing worth attention. It stuck in my mind while, in persuasive tones, and with airy fluency, he discoursed of the profits that could be made, nowadays, in arming privateers under the Mexican flag. He told me I needn’t be surprised at their being fitted out in a Spanish colony.

===Chinese===

“我们高贵的朋友”——他用一只白胖的手朝卡洛斯轻轻一挥——“已经告诉过我，您是何等样胆大包天的豪杰；为了搭救落难的朋友，把半数弓街缉私吏的脑袋都敲开了。好，我敬佩您；我自己也干过一样的。”他补一句，“那是当年了，”叹了口气。

“您是说九八年，”我说，略带无礼。

奥布赖恩眼睛一亮。事实上，在爱尔兰那场惨败裡他差点丢了脖子——不是在克朗梅尔就是在斯莱戈——在雾裡从英国龙骑兵手下狂奔，逃进湾裡一条法国军舰的小艇。对他来说，哪怕如今他已是古巴（Cuba）的法官，那也是青春的英雄篇章——事实上，是罗曼斯。所以，多半他并不恼我提起它。我倒确实想恼火他话音裡某种轻慢、神气裡某种居高临下。

老堂安睡着，脸朝着远处污黑的天花板。

“这样吧，我给您出个公道的价，”奥布赖恩忽然说，此前他对我不逊的目光做了一番专注的研究。我不喜欢他，因为我全然不知他是哪一号人。事实上，他比卡洛斯还让我陌生。他给我的印象是：纵然他未必绝对胜过我，他仍能耍弄我，或者至少叫我显得像个傻子。

“听说您是分离派，”他说。“呢，这像我。我是爱尔兰人；在另一个岛上，我的脑袋上悬过赏格。而这裡为了殴打上将，正对您发着拘票。我们可以合作，我替您想的事裡没有任何下贱的成分。”

他屡次听卡洛斯说起，我是个亡命而目无法纪的贵族青年，住在一个全然听凭亡命杀人的走私贩子摆布的地方。可是在牙买加（Jamaica）有拘票对付我，这是我头一回确切听到。无疑，这是拉蒙说的，那家伙无所不知。这个刻薄的小爱尔兰人对我说的一切裡，这似乎是唯一值得留意的。它钉在我脑子裡，与此同时，他用劝诱的口吻、轻盈的流利，讲起如今在墨西哥旗下武装私掠船能赚的种种好处。他告诉我，不必为它们在西班牙殖民地装备出航而惊讶。

===Original===

“There’s more than one aspect to disloyalty like this,” said he dispassionately, but with a quick wink contrasting with his tone.
Spain resented our recognition of their rebellious colonies. And with the same cool persuasiveness, relieved by humorous smiles, he explained that the loyal Spaniards of the Ever Faithful Island thought there was no sin in doing harm to the English, even under the Mexican flag, whose legal existence they did not recognize.
“Mind ye, it’s an organized thing, I have something to say in it. It hurts Mr. Canning’s Government at home, the curse of Cromwell on him and them. They will be dropping some of their own colonies directly. And as you are a Separationist, small blame to you, and I am an Irishman, we shan’t cry our eyes out over it. Come, Mr. Kemp, ’tis all for the good of the Cause.﻿ ﻿… And there’s nothing *low*. You are a gentleman, and I wouldn’t propose anything that was. The very best people in Havana are interested in the matter. Our schooners lie in Rio Medio, but I can’t be there all the time myself.”
Surprise deprived me of speech. I glanced at Carlos. He was watching us inscrutably. The young girl touched the lizard gently, but it was too frightened to move. O’Brien, with shrewd glances, rocked his chair.﻿ ﻿… What did I want? he inquired. To see life? What he proposed was the life for a fine young fellow like me. Moreover, I was half Scotch. Had I forgotten the wrongs of my own country? Had I forgotten the ’45?
“You’ll have heard tell of a Scotch Chief Justice whose son spent in Amsterdam the money his father earned on the justice seat in Edinb’ro’﻿—money paid for rum and run silks﻿ ﻿…”
Of course I had heard of it; everybody had; but it had been some years before.
“We’re backwards hereabouts,” O’Brien jeered. “But over there they winked and chuckled at the judge, and they do the same in Havana at us.”
Suddenly from behind us the voice of the young girl said, “Of what do you discourse, my English cousin?”
O’Brien interposed deferentially. “Señorita, I ask him to come to Rio,” he said.
She turned her large dark eyes scrutinizingly upon me, then dropped them again. She was arranging some melon seeds in a rayed circle round the lizard that looked motionlessly at her.
“Do not speak very loudly, lest you awaken my father,” she warned us.
The old Don’s face was still turned to the ceiling.

===Chinese===

“这种不忠有一张以上的面孔，”他不带感情地说，却飞快眨了一下眼，同语气两样。

西班牙怨着我们承认他们叛乱的殖民地。他带着同样冷静的说服力，间或用幽默的微笑调剂，解释说，“永贞之岛”上忠顺的西班牙人认为，伤害英国人不算罪过，哪怕打着墨西哥的旗——那旗子的合法存在他们本就不认。

“您听着，这是有组织的买卖，我在裡头说得上话。它刺痛坎宁先生在国内的政府，叫克伦威尔的诅咒降到他和他那帮人头上。他们眼看就要丢掉自己的一些殖民地了。您是分离派，难怪您；我是爱尔兰人；我们都不会为这个哭瞎眼睛。来吧，肯普先生，这全是为了我们的事业。……而且没有任何下贱的成分。您是绅士，我不会提任何配不上绅士的事。哈瓦那（Havana）最上等的人都沾着这桩事。我们的纵帆船泊在裡奥梅迪奥（Rio Medio），可我自己不能常在那儿。”

惊愕夺去了我的言语。我瞥了一眼卡洛斯。他莫测地看着我们。年轻的姑娘轻轻碰了碰蜥蜴，它却怕得动也不动。奥布赖恩目光精明，摇着他的椅子。……我想要什么？他问。见识生活？他提的正是配我这样一个好青年的生活。况且，我有半个苏格兰。难道我忘了自己祖国的冤屈？难道我忘了四五年的事？

“您总听说过一位苏格兰首席法官吧，他儿子把父亲在爱丁堡法官席上挣的钱花在了阿姆斯特丹——那是朗姆酒和走私丝绸付的账……”

当然听说过；人人都听说过；只是那是好些年前的事了。

“我们这一带落后，”奥布赖恩讥笑。“可在那边，他们对那位法官挤眼睛、笑嘻嘻；在哈瓦那，人家对我们也一样。”

忽然，背后响起年轻姑娘的声音：“你们在谈论什么，我的英国表兄？”

奥布赖恩恭敬地插话。“小姐，我请他到裡奥去，”他说。

她把大大的黑眼睛审视地转向我，又垂下去。她正把几粒瓜子围着蜥蜴摆成一个放射的圈，蜥蜴一动不动地望着她。

“不要太大声说话，免得吵醒我的父亲，”她告诫我们。

老堂的脸仍然朝着天花板。

===Original===

Carlos, standing behind his chair, opened his mouth a little in a half smile. I was really angry with O’Brien by that time, with his air of omniscience, superiority, and self-content, as if he were talking to a child or someone very credulous and weak-minded.
“What right have you to speak for me, Señor Juez?” I said in the best Spanish I could.
The young girl looked at me once more, and then again looked down.
“Oh, I can speak for you,” he answered in English, “because I know. Your position’s this.” He sat down in his rocking chair, crossed his legs, and looked at me as if he expected me to show signs of astonishment at his knowing so much. “You’re in a hole. You must leave this island of Jamaica﻿—surely it’s as distressful as my own dear land﻿—and you can’t go home, because the runners would be after you. You’re ‘wanted’ here as well as there, and you’ve nowhere to go.”
I looked at him, quite startled by this view of my case. He extended one plump hand towards me, and still further lowered his voice.
“Now, I offer you a good berth, a snug berth. And ’tis a pretty spot.” He got a sort of languorous honey into his voice, and drawled out, “The﻿—the Señorita’s.” He took an air of businesslike candour. “You can help us, and we you; we could do without you better than you without us. Our undertaking﻿—there’s big names in it, just as in the Free Trading you know so well, don’t be saying you don’t﻿—is worked from Havana. What we need is a man we can trust. We had one﻿—Nichols. You remember the mate of the ship you came over in. He was Nicola el Demonio; he won’t be any longer﻿—I can’t tell you why, it’s too long a story.”
I did remember very vividly that cadaverous Nova Scotian mate of the *Thames*, who had warned me with truculent menaces against showing my face in Rio Medio. I remembered his sallow, shiny cheeks, and the exaggerated gestures of his claw-like hands.
O’Brien smiled. “Nichols is alive right enough, but no more good than if he were dead. And that’s the truth. He pretends his nerve’s gone; he was a devil among tailors for a time, but he’s taken to crying now. It was when your blundering old admiral’s boats had to be beaten off that his zeal cooled. He thinks the British Government will rise in its strength.” There was a bitter contempt in his voice, but he regained his calm business tone. “It will do nothing of the sort.

“您有什么权利替我说话，法官先生？”我用我最好的西班牙语说。
